history.p: Gade started working on his second symphony shortly after the C minor symphony had had its first performance in Leipzig in March 1843. He brought the manuscript with him when he in September embarked on his European tour and finished the score in Leipzig November that year. It had its first performance in the Gewandhaus on 18 January 1844 and was well received, but never gained the same popularity as the first symphony.

physDesc.physMedium: 5 single folios. Written in ink. Paper: 10 staves. Paginated in foreign hand. A few figured bass and instrument indications. Sketch for the first movement on pp. 1-5; heading on p. 1: "Sinf. N 2". dated "13. Maj 1843". At the end of the first movement on p. 5 dated "18. Maj 1843". Sketch for the second movement on pp. 6-7 dated "19. [July in runes]. On pp. 8-10 the first 282 bars of the third movement. The remaining bars of the sketch are found in DK-Kk, C II, 6 Gades Samling 396 .

3 bifolios. Written in ink. Paper: 10 staves. The first 8 pages contains sketches for the end of the 3rd movement (from bar 283) and the entire 4th movement. The sketches are notated in piano score with a few figured bass and instrument indications. Many corrections, a small number of which are written in pencil. On p. 7 end-dated "Fine" ['October Leipzig' inscribed in runes] .The remaining pages contain the songs: "Reiselied" (NWGW 276); "Sehnsucht" (NWGW A 32); "Der Hidalgo" (NWGW A 46): "Der Zigeunerbube im Norden" (NWGW A 47); "Frühling und Liebe" (NWGW 280); and "Maifeier" (NWGW 277).

physDesc.physMedium: Bound in dark green cloth with "Sinfonia N.W. Gade" stamped in gold on the spine. Written in ink. Paper: 20 staves. At the top of the title page is written "Autograph" in foreign hand. At the end of the first movement on p. 32 dated "XVI.[June in runes] 1843". At the end of the second movement on p. 43 dated "XXIII. [July in runes]". At the general rest bars 289-292 dated "XXI. [August in runes]". The transition to the 4th movement is marked with a double bar-line and the new tempo, but there is no "Finale" inscription. At the end of the music dated "Fine / Leipzig / 1843 XX. [November in runes]".
